items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: I could have got him Gardena, Giardina, Tony Giardina was around New York doing nothing.

ctx.x: Yes that's right. We'll keep it now. This is a letter from Emil Christian and it says I would like Philip Napoleon on cornet and Johnny Costello on clarinet. The boys I was working with because they have more of an idea what I want and they can play all the Dixieland numbers because I'll know we'll get some requests for them. It's signed on the back here. Sincerely, Emil Christian, 2 Bagley Street, Tidingham Court Road, Apartment 1, London, England. And I don't see the date. Let me think. It's on the 1st. The…

Now from this letter you'll see this is a New Orleans man. I could have had him shopping. I could have got him Gardena, Giardina, Tony Giardina was around New York doing nothing. And I had contacted these men finally. But he wanted men who copied from the Dixieland records. We'll go to show you that even the New Orleans boys didn't want the boys from New Orleans because they didn't know the rhythm. That is the truth that I am sitting here and telling you that no New Orleans band played the rhythm that was…

I hate to interrupt you on that story but I missed out a couple of things. I didn't get who was in the band at the time. I know Edwards was back. He replaced Christian and I didn't get the names of the other bands.
